picks.title: How much?? Chinese startup unveils copper-colored AI Max+ PRO 495 workstation with 192GB RAM selling for a cool $6,800 — TOPC TXA2 can take 4 SSDs and drives 4 8K monitors
picks.rationale: New product: TOPC's TXA2 is a 192GB Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 local-AI workstation priced at about $6,800 that drives four 8K monitors. It shows what desk-side AI hardware costs while RAM prices are spiking.
picks.excerpt: Obscure brand wants nearly $6,800 for its copper-colored AI workstation

picks.title: Gemini for Android rolls out side panel and settings redesign
picks.rationale: New release: the Gemini Android app ships a redesigned side panel and settings screen right after the Spark-to-Task update. It is a live reference for how Google is restructuring navigation in an assistant app.
picks.excerpt: Following the Spark-to-Task update, the Gemini app has now rolled out redesigns of the side panel and settings on Android.

picks.title: Nvidia's DGX Spark can now join forces with seven others to deliver 1 TB of memory
picks.rationale: New announcement from GTC Berlin: DGX Spark clustering now goes up to eight units for 1 TB of unified memory, and Nvidia claims up to 40% faster agentic inference on select RTX hardware. Desk-scale local AI capacity just took a big step up.
picks.excerpt: Nvidia has expanded DGX Spark's clustering capabilities, allowing users to connect up to eight systems for a combined 1 TB of unified memory. The company has also announced inference optimisations promising up to 40% faster agentic AI workloads on select RTX hardware, alongside improvements for DGX

picks.title: This crowdfunded $109 hub wants to pool the RAM in your old PCs, Macs, and phones to run bigger AI models — but the engine underneath is software you can already get for free
picks.rationale: New product: the RAMDeck hub pools memory from your idle devices to run larger local models while DDR5 prices are spiking. TechRadar notes it is slow and that the underlying engine is free software, which makes it a useful reality check.
picks.excerpt: Can't stomach DDR5 at five times last year's price? RAMDeck wants to borrow your other devices' memory instead, and it admits that won't be fast.

picks.title: Someone turned their monitor into a laser pointer firing range game using Claude Code
picks.rationale: New maker project: a webcam and laser pointer turn an ordinary monitor into a light-gun-style shooting range, built with Claude Code. It shows AI coding agents being used to prototype physical-interaction hardware quickly.
picks.excerpt: It's like a light gun game, but with lasers.
